BLOCKER: `scripts/dev/gate0_check.py` is created `mode 100644` with no shebang, yet invoked as an executable by both `precheck.py` (`subprocess.run(["scripts/dev/gate0_check.py"])`) and `ci-cd-gates.json` → EACCES/ENOEXEC; precheck catches only `FileNotFoundError`, so the run crashes instead of gating.

Required AC tests are absent: no tests for gate0 negative/positive, SCOPE resolution, accepted-risk validation, or duplicate-review refusal (only new Go store/policy tests are present) → "Tests: ... precheck PASS" unmet.
`accepted_risks {owner, until, rationale}` validation demanded by AC is not implemented anywhere in `gate_decide.py`/`gate_decisions.py`.
AC "gate_decide ... refuses in CI" is unimplemented (no CI-environment detection); `--hil-confirmed` is a self-asserted CLI flag, so the human-only control is not enforceable.

SCOPE handling is only an enum addition (`DISPOSITION_STATUSES += "SCOPE"`); there is no approval-path check that SCOPE findings reference a follow-up item nor the "cannot block approved delivery" guard.
AC "gate-brief renders the same reconciliation/impact table for HIL" has no corresponding change; `render()` is only used inside `gate0_check.py`.
MAJOR: `gate0_check.transitions()` swallows JSON/`git show` failures with `continue` (fail-open) and only scans `merge-base develop..HEAD`, so malformed items or uncommitted local status flips bypass Gate 0 — violates the fail-closed standard.

`go_modules_check._changed_modules` scoping weakens an existing gate: `git status --porcelain` untracked lines (`?? product-forge/go/...`) are never normalized, so newly added Go files are missed and their module is skipped (gofmt/vet/tests silently not run).

precheck fast tier now skips Python tests entirely when no `.py` changed and never runs the full suite by default (old `pipeline-tests-full` removed) — a coverage regression; `_SMOKE`/`_test_files` must exist or `_smoke_tests()` raises NameError.
`LocalStore.keyLocks` grows one mutex per key forever (unbounded memory in a long-lived process) and is held for the entire streaming `Put`, serializing large uploads per key.

`objreconcile.Scan` excludes `invalid` manifest keys from orphan detection, so a real store object matching a duplicate/out-of-prefix manifest entry is neither orphaned nor expected → silently unreported drift.
Duplicate-review refusal keys only on `EVID/{item}-{sha}.json` and does not cover the `ingest` path, so a second review can still be recorded for the same immutable sha.
MINOR: `S3Store.Capabilities` takes/releases the same mutex twice; probes are one-shot at `New`, so capabilities can be stale if bucket lock/versioning changes later.
API/AC row detection uses substring matching (`"api" in claims`) — false positives/negatives on claim wording; no structured claim type.
New Go packages log via stdlib `log` (objpolicy/objreconcile/s3store) rather than the project's structured logging → weak observability/alerting hooks.
No ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS/ADR entry for the BI-PF-1471 gate governance changes (the only doc addition, EDP-16, belongs to a different item).
Confirm `gate0_check.py` qualifies as "tooling Python" under the language rule, since it encodes new shipped enforcement logic.
NIT: Stray trailing blank line added at end of `go_modules_check.py`.
`S3Store.probeLock` logs a probe failure for every store construction even when object lock is never used (log noise).
SUMMARY: Solid Go-side work on lifecycle/signed-URL/reconciliation, but the BI-PF-1471 acceptance criteria are largely unmet: gate0 itself cannot execute as wired, and the HIL-only, CI-refusal, accepted-risk, SCOPE, gate-brief, and required-test items are missing or stub-level.
Top risks: gates that fail to run (fail-open delivery), human-only decisions enforceable by a flag alone, and a Go test-gate scoping bug that silently skips new modules.
